newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply against the dollar on Wednesday in active trading as the business sector converted dollars into shekels, dealers said.
"The shekel started rising on Tuesday after the setting of the representative rate and this trend continued today," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
He added that activity was relatively high.
Dealers said companies were selling dollars on expectations the shekel will continue to appreciate in the near future against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies.
"I believe that this trend will continue in the near term and the shekel will soon test the 3.5 shekels per dollar level," one dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5140 shekels compared with 3.5300 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7729 against 3.7952 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 3.0517 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0431 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9207 shekels compared with 1.9473 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5150 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
